records.name: Hope for Wellness Help Line
records.what: Counselling and crisis help by phone or online chat, 24 hours a day, for Indigenous people anywhere in Canada.
records.start: Call 1-855-242-3310, or open the chat on the website.

records.name: 9-8-8 Suicide Crisis Helpline
records.what: Call or text 988 any time if you are thinking about suicide or worried about someone. Free, in every province and territory.
records.start: Call or text 988. In an emergency, call 911.

records.name: National Indian Residential School Crisis Line
records.what: Crisis support, 24 hours a day, for former residential school students and their families, with referrals to other health supports.
records.who: Former Indian Residential School students and their families.

records.name: Jordan's Principle
records.what: Funding so First Nations children can get the health, social and education products, services and supports they need, on or off reserve. Named for Jordan River Anderson of Norway House Cree Nation.
records.start: Call the Jordan's Principle Call Centre, open 24 hours. It is not a crisis line; if a child needs immediate care, call 911.

records.name: Inuit Child First Initiative
records.what: Funding so Inuit children have equal access to health, social and education products, services and supports. Free to apply.
records.who: Inuit children, wherever they live in Canada.
records.start: Contact your regional focal point, or call the national call centre, open 24 hours.

records.name: Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB)
records.what: Federal coverage for health costs that provincial plans and private insurance do not cover, such as prescription drugs, dental and vision care, medical supplies, mental health counselling and medical travel.
records.who: Residents of Canada who are registered First Nations or recognized Inuit. First Nations in British Columbia are covered through the First Nations Health Authority instead, and Inuit in Nunavik through their regional board.
records.start: Read who is eligible, then ask your health provider or pharmacist to bill NIHB.

records.name: Friendship Centres
records.what: Community hubs for Indigenous people living in cities and towns, with programs in health, shelter, youth, justice and more. Over 100 centres belong to the National Association of Friendship Centres.
records.who: Indigenous people living in urban areas; many programs are open to everyone.
records.start: Find the centre nearest you on the association's map.
